searchText: please ping me or entire group Ethproofs call #2—real-time proving (starting in ~15 min) Zoom link: https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/8286061638?pwd=YmprOHJOZWlFQW8wSEVFVEVQanFvQT09, Agenda: newly open-sourced zkVMs [redacted], , newly tracked zkVMs Ligetron: Muthu Venkitasubramaniam, Miden VM: Bobbin Threadbare, Nock VM: Logan Allen, SP1 Hypercube: Ron Rothblum, , EFer updates RTP grants: Alex Hicks, killers: Ignacio Hagopian, killers killer: Julian Ma, zk-boost: Kev Wedderburn, Ethproofs V2: Justin Drake, , real-time proving Succinct: John Guibas, RISC Zero: Jeremy Bruestle, ZisK: Jordi Baylina, Brevis: Mo Dong, ZKM: Stephen Duan, Snarkify: Ouyang Jiannan, , GPU proving [Ingonyama], Supranational: Kelly Olson, ZAN: Guiming Wu, , ASIC proving Accseal: Mingyu Gao, Cysic: Leo Fan, Fabric: Michael Gao, Intchains: Hugo Tsai, Irreducible: Radi Cojbasic, Ponos: Slobodan Lukovic, , distributed proving Fermah: Vanishree Rao, ZkCloud: Norbert Vadas Charging according to how parallelizible a tx is..? https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.11964 Step 1: BAL. Analysis Step 2: FPE (Fee market for parallel execution). are you guys in touch with RPC providers? cc <@372731338031366165> and probably <@97774605351010304> (the only ones I know of). I know first hand that when Arbitrum started looking into better pricing for Stylus that enabled a lot more computation than the EVM, they looked into paralellization. The problem was that some operators are already fully parallelized and would actually be hit hard with such a change. Now on the L2 world where only some nodes are needed to be running and the percentage of RPC-serving nodes is higher and are already running fully paralellized, it makes sense to not make it cheaper to run in paralllel. On L1 in principle I could see why the situation would be drastically different, but still I believe RPC providers should be part of this conversation
